AC-01.6.2 contradicts AC-01.6.3. In the example, after HR records that Tomás's wife no longer lives in Switzerland, the expected result for Denomination is 'asked'. But the employee can no longer answer anything after submission (AC-01.6.1), and AC-01.6.3 / D-048 say the tariff code should then show 'incomplete - HR must complete'. Which is the expected outcome for this example: is the employee asked again (the questionnaire reopens for them), or does HR complete it while the result shows 'incomplete'?

For a Liechtenstein resident with more than 45 non-return days, AC-06.6.3 and the tariff code rule say the code is recorded 'with the note subject to the double taxation agreement', but the example expects just 'C0Y' and D-051 says the code is one single text. Is the note part of the recorded result text (e.g. 'C0Y, subject to the double taxation agreement'), or is the code 'C0Y' recorded alone with the note and HR flag kept separately? This changes what is recorded and what the acceptance test checks.

"(The expression gives, per child, whether that child is counted; the digit is the number of children for which it is true.)" - Refers to an internal formula ('expression') rather than business language. D-045 forbids this.

"(The expression gives, per child, whether that child is counted; the digit is the number of children for which it is true.)" - Refers to an internal formula ('expression') rather than business language. D-045 forbids this.

"using only the constructs the condition language allows; the child digit is 1 when the child counts, otherwise 0." - D-052 (in the Evidence list) refers to the constraints of an internal rule/condition language. That is an implementation detail, not a business rule.

info.message: The first working day 'must lie within one year after the questionnaire is sent'. Can it also be before the send date or in the past, for example when the employee has already started or fills in the questionnaire late? Sending the questionnaire is part of the later HR-side spec, so which date counts as 'sent' for this check? Is there also any plausibility check on the spouse's date of birth?

The stories disagree on when a missing required answer blocks the employee. US-02.1 and US-02.2 say the employee 'cannot continue' to the next step. US-04.1 and AC-01.8.3 say the employee only cannot submit, and is then shown what is missing. Should a missing required answer stop the employee from moving to the next step, or only from submitting (so a partly filled step can be saved and left, as US-01.7 allows)?

The item is called 'Certificate of residence handed in', and the calculator asks whether it has been provided ('beigebracht'). The story instead asks whether the employee 'has a certificate of residence for HR'. Does 'yes' mean the certificate has already been given to HR, or only that the employee has one? Should HR expect a certificate later for 'no' as well as for 'not yet', or only for 'not yet'?

Expected results for the same question differ between stories. US-01.2 marks spouse's nationality, spouse lives in Switzerland and nationality as 'asked' (AC-01.2.4, AC-01.2.5). US-05.1 and US-05.2 mark the same cases as 'required'. Several rows also show '–' for questions that always apply, for example civil status for the married C-permit holder in AC-01.2.5, or postcode and town for Stefan in AC-01.2.3. Is there a real difference between 'asked' and 'required' (can any of these answers be left empty?), and does '–' mean 'not checked in this example'?

In the AC-06.6.3 example table, the columns for whether denomination, spouse gainfully employed and has children were asked show '–' for the 'at most 45 non-return days' and 'more than 45 non-return days' rows, rather than 'not asked' or 'asked' as in the 'returns daily' row. Should the expected values be 'not asked' for the second row and 'asked' for the third, so these examples can be tested?

D-052 (cited for the source tax tariff code rule) says 'the child digit is 1 when the child counts, otherwise 0'. The child digit rule and F-zh_source_tax_calculator-4c53e3 say the digit is the number of counted children (e.g. C3Y). Can you confirm that D-052 means the per-child contribution and that the code's digit is the total count, with no upper limit (D-044)?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Okay, that's fine, the calculator will tell us. I think I have what I need. Is there anything you were hoping to cover that we didn't?
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

questions.question: AC-01.6.2 contradicts AC-01.6.3. In the example, after HR records that Tomás's wife no longer lives in Switzerland, the expected result for Denomination is 'asked'. But the employee can no longer answer anything after submission (AC-01.6.1), and AC-01.6.3 / D-048 say the tariff code should then show 'incomplete - HR must complete'. Which is the expected outcome for this example: is the employee asked again (the questionnaire reopens for them), or does HR complete it while the result shows 'incomplete'?

The first working day 'must lie within one year after the questionnaire is sent'. Can it also be before the send date or in the past, for example when the employee has already started or fills in the questionnaire late? Sending the questionnaire is part of the later HR-side spec, so which date counts as 'sent' for this check? Is there also any plausibility check on the spouse's date of birth?

The stories disagree on when a missing required answer blocks the employee. US-02.1 and US-02.2 say the employee 'cannot continue' to the next step. US-04.1 and AC-01.8.3 say the employee only cannot submit, and is then shown what is missing. Should a missing required answer stop the employee from moving to the next step, or only from submitting (so a partly filled step can be saved and left, as US-01.7 allows)?

The item is called 'Certificate of residence handed in', and the calculator asks whether it has been provided ('beigebracht'). The story instead asks whether the employee 'has a certificate of residence for HR'. Does 'yes' mean the certificate has already been given to HR, or only that the employee has one? Should HR expect a certificate later for 'no' as well as for 'not yet', or only for 'not yet'?

Expected results for the same question differ between stories. US-01.2 marks spouse's nationality, spouse lives in Switzerland and nationality as 'asked' (AC-01.2.4, AC-01.2.5). US-05.1 and US-05.2 mark the same cases as 'required'. Several rows also show '–' for questions that always apply, for example civil status for the married C-permit holder in AC-01.2.5, or postcode and town for Stefan in AC-01.2.3. Is there a real difference between 'asked' and 'required' (can any of these answers be left empty?), and does '–' mean 'not checked in this example'?

For a Liechtenstein resident with more than 45 non-return days, AC-06.6.3 and the tariff code rule say the code is recorded 'with the note subject to the double taxation agreement', but the example expects just 'C0Y' and D-051 says the code is one single text. Is the note part of the recorded result text (e.g. 'C0Y, subject to the double taxation agreement'), or is the code 'C0Y' recorded alone with the note and HR flag kept separately? This changes what is recorded and what the acceptance test checks.

In the AC-06.6.3 example table, the columns for whether denomination, spouse gainfully employed and has children were asked show '–' for the 'at most 45 non-return days' and 'more than 45 non-return days' rows, rather than 'not asked' or 'asked' as in the 'returns daily' row. Should the expected values be 'not asked' for the second row and 'asked' for the third, so these examples can be tested?

D-052 (cited for the source tax tariff code rule) says 'the child digit is 1 when the child counts, otherwise 0'. The child digit rule and F-zh_source_tax_calculator-4c53e3 say the digit is the number of counted children (e.g. C3Y). Can you confirm that D-052 means the per-child contribution and that the code's digit is the total count, with no upper limit (D-044)?

review.summary: All 300+ examples pass and there are no errors. Two major dev-refinement questions are open (AC-01.6.2 vs AC-01.6.3, and the Liechtenstein tariff-code note), and implementation vocabulary leaks into the spec (D-045 and D-052 'expression' / 'condition language', ISO 3166). Many trace-judge partials also point to non-cited or unbacked claims. Resolve the blockers, then it should be ready_with_caveats.

findings.title: AC-01.6.2 contradicts AC-01.6.3 after submission
findings.why: The example expects Denomination 'asked' after HR records a change, but the questionnaire is read-only after submission and the tariff code should show 'incomplete - HR must complete'. Devs cannot tell whether the questionnaire reopens.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) US-01.6; AC-01.6.1/2/3; D-048; example 'AC-01.6.2 / Tomás after HR records...'
findings.action: Add a decision: after submission HR completes the missing answers and the tariff shows incomplete (no reopen), or the questionnaire reopens for the employee. Fix the AC-01.6.2 expected value to match.

findings.title: Liechtenstein >45 days: is the DTA note part of the recorded code?
findings.why: The recorded result changes. The example expects 'C0Y' alone, the rule says 'with the note', and D-051 says the code is one single text. The acceptance test is ambiguous.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) US-06.6; AC-06.6.3; rule.tariff_code trace_judge (expression lacks the note/flag); D-051
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml: code 'C0Y' with the note and HR flag stored separately, or one text including the note. Align the rule expression, the AC and the examples.

findings.title: Technical vocabulary leaks into the spec
findings.why: The spec must stay in business language. D-045 forbids 'expression', and D-052 refers to the 'condition language'.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: information.md and feature.md ('The expression gives, per child...'; D-052 'constructs the condition language allows'); ISO 3166 in item.address_country, item.nationality, item.spouse_nationality, AC-02.3.1
findings.action: Reword to business language, e.g. 'the digit is the number of counted children' and 'country list (all countries, plus stateless)'. Reword D-052 and remove the ISO standard name unless the PO wants it as a requirement.

findings.title: Child digit wording in D-052 conflicts with the rule
findings.why: D-052 says the digit is 1 or 0, but the rule and calculator say the digit is the count of counted children (C3Y), with no upper limit (D-044).
findings.action: Confirm that D-052 means the per-child contribution and reword it. State the total count and no upper limit.

findings.title: Rules and ACs rest on uncited or unbacked claims
findings.why: Traceability is partial. Several claims have no cited fact: the Liechtenstein 'never cross-border' claim, Swiss nationals being exempt, the spouse-employment and children conditions for Liechtenstein, the Maria/Tomás example refs, and the partner date of birth for Separated.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: rule.cross_border_tariff, US-08.2, US-06.5, US-06.6, US-06.2/06.3/06.7, US-01.2/01.4, rule.pension_fund_civil_status, item.spouse_gainful_employment, item.has_children
findings.action: Add the missing fact citations (F-hr_transcript-845204, -b90bd9, -3f2c2a, F-...-cc19c7) or record decisions. Confirm the partner date of birth for Separated and Married, and the Liechtenstein daily-return case.

findings.title: Required vs asked, and '–' in example tables are inconsistent
findings.why: The same cases are marked 'asked' in US-01.2 and 'required' in US-05.x. '–' is used for questions that always apply. The AC-06.6.3 rows are untestable as written.
findings.action: Define 'asked' vs 'required' in guidance. Fill in the '–' cells with explicit expected values (not asked / asked).

findings.title: Missing-answer behaviour: blocks the step or only the submit?
findings.why: US-02.x says the employee cannot continue. US-04.1 and AC-01.8.3 say only submit is blocked. This conflicts with the save-and-resume in US-01.7.
findings.action: Decide: block only submit (recommended, matches US-01.7) and update US-02.1 and US-02.2.

findings.title: Certificate of residence semantics unclear
findings.why: The item says 'handed in', the calculator says provided ('beigebracht'), and the story says the employee 'has' one. HR's follow-up for 'no' vs 'not yet' is undefined.
findings.action: Decide what 'yes' means and whether HR expects a certificate for 'no' or only for 'not yet'.
